camps.name: Lunch Bar
camps.desc: Small sloping sandy camp with early shade; better at low water.

camps.name: Upper Horse Creek
camps.desc: Tree-covered camp upstream of the creek.

camps.name: Lower Horse Creek
camps.desc: Low-water bar with a difficult landing.

camps.name: Bridge Piling
camps.desc: Best at low water. Pilings from a pack bridge removed in 1970 are nearby.

camps.name: Legend Creek
camps.desc: Small beach with an easy landing. Pictographs about 500 yards upstream. Watch for poison ivy.

camps.name: Spindle Creek
camps.desc: Sloped beach with tent sites above. Stone ruins from a 1950s settler nearby.

camps.name: Phantom
camps.desc: Grows as the water drops; the upper beach is larger. Just above Ranier Rapid.

camps.name: Alder Creek
camps.desc: Comfortable at low water. The first reservable camp on the Main.

camps.name: Otter Beach
camps.desc: Small low-water camp at the end of slow water; shaded.

camps.name: Fawn Creek
camps.desc: Shaded camp on the bench.

camps.name: Upper Lantz
camps.desc: Among trees on the bench. Better access at medium to high water.

camps.name: Lower Lantz Bar
camps.desc: Large bar above a sandy beach, just above Lantz Rapid.

camps.name: Tag Creek
camps.desc: Just below Lantz Rapid. Fine at high water; a rocky climb at low water. Shaded.

camps.name: Eddy Beach
camps.desc: Small low-water beach.

camps.name: Disappointment Creek
camps.desc: High-bench camp; a strenuous climb in summer heat.

camps.name: Upper Devil's Teeth
camps.desc: Reservable pebble beach just above the rapid. Often missed.

camps.name: Lower Devil's Teeth
camps.desc: Large, pleasant reservable camp. Pictographs about 100 yards downstream.

camps.name: Overhang (Hangover)
camps.desc: Small low-water camp, visible from upriver.

camps.name: Elkhorn
camps.desc: Large, pretty camp on the bank.

camps.name: Chamberlain Creek
camps.desc: Small camp for low flows. A trail leads up to Chamberlain Basin.

camps.name: Chuckar Beach
camps.desc: Medium low-water beach camp.

camps.name: Blackadar
camps.desc: Large reservable camp on a high bench in a ponderosa grove. Named for Dr. Walt Blackadar.

camps.name: Motor Camp
camps.desc: Mainly a low-water camp, large and reservable. Look for the engine in camp.

camps.name: Guth Cabins
camps.desc: Reservable low-water camp about a quarter mile below the creek, at the site of the original Guth cabins.

camps.name: Black Canyon Beach
camps.desc: Small campsite with an easy beach landing and views upstream.

camps.name: Sunny Bar
camps.desc: Rocky landing and a medium carry to a shaded ponderosa bench. Hot springs may be reachable at low water.

camps.name: Hot Spring
camps.desc: Just around the corner from the hot springs. Strong current and rocks make landing hard.

camps.name: Sandy Hole
camps.desc: Small camp; a good lunch stop after the hot springs.

camps.name: Poor Bar
camps.desc: Good high-water camp. The Forest Service lists capacity for 30 people.

camps.name: Bruin Bar
camps.desc: Excellent reservable camp with a difficult landing at high flows.

camps.name: Hancock
camps.desc: Reservable, immediately below the rapid. At high flows work left early to reach the landing.

camps.name: Magpie
camps.desc: Large and popular; burned in a 2023 wildfire, so shade may be limited.

camps.name: Bargamin
camps.desc: About 50 yards below the creek. High-water bench with a small low-water beach. Easy hike to scout Bailey Rapid.

camps.name: Bailey Bar
camps.desc: Reservable low-water camp with a nice beach. Popular lunch stop.

camps.name: Upper Yellow Pine
camps.desc: Large camp with a trail to view Big Mallard. A wire from a 1940s crank phone system is visible.

camps.name: Lower Yellow Pine
camps.desc: Large reservable camp with a low-water sandy beach.

camps.name: Big Mallard
camps.desc: Large reservable camp just below Mallard Creek.

camps.name: Easter Egg Beach
camps.desc: Beach below the rock outcropping, across from Jim Moore's.

camps.name: Jim Moore's
camps.desc: Reservable mix of beach and cobble; a shared beach.

camps.name: Groundhog Bar
camps.desc: Large reservable camp; not accessible at high flows. Catch the eddy in front of the rock.

camps.name: Reed Creek
camps.desc: Large reservable camp with a pretty creek upstream.

camps.name: Rhett Creek
camps.desc: Large, exposed, reservable camp.

camps.name: Paine Creek
camps.desc: Small reserved camp with a sandy beach at the base of a cliff.

camps.name: No Man's Beach
camps.desc: Small, rocky-sandy, no shade; little used.

camps.name: Teepee
camps.desc: Small reservable camp. A grave marker for Jack Ranger, who drowned here in 1928.

camps.name: Pebble Beach
camps.desc: Pretty camp, often steep at low water. Small groups.

camps.name: Haynie Bar
camps.desc: Large reservable camp. Look for the big boulder on shore.

camps.name: Wilson Bar (Jackson Bar)
camps.desc: Less desirable. The public airstrip is here.

camps.name: Mackay Bar Bridge
camps.desc: Reservable; trucks are often parked here from Painter Mine Road.

camps.name: Deadman's Hole
camps.desc: Small camp; may hear air traffic from Mackay Bar.

camps.name: South Fork Island
camps.desc: Low-water camp at the bottom of the island. Watch for the eddy.

camps.name: Mann Creek
camps.desc: Reservable.

camps.name: Warren Creek
camps.desc: Reservable.

camps.name: Swimming Hole (Warren Bar)
camps.desc: Reservable.

camps.name: Indian Creek
camps.desc: Nice camp downstream of the creek. A shady trail leads to Indian Creek Ranch.

camps.name: Rabbit Creek
camps.desc: Reservable.

camps.name: Basin Creek
camps.desc: No shade; hot.

camps.name: Upper Bull Creek
camps.desc: Reservable; a hot camp.

camps.name: Lower Bull Creek
camps.desc: Sandy beach with a short carry. Large group camp with a spring. Poison ivy near the creek.

camps.name: Gold Rush Bar
camps.desc: Small beach that changes yearly; cobble landing.

camps.name: California Creek
camps.desc: Large, popular reservable camp with a sprawling beach.

camps.name: T-Bone
camps.desc: Low-water beach; reservable.

camps.name: Maxwell Bar
camps.desc: Large reservable beach with little shade. A sand dune for jumping into the river; good for kids.

camps.name: Johnson Creek
camps.desc: Reservable.

rapids.name: Killam Rapid
rapids.desc: Rocks and tricky current; the first swim of the trip for inflatable kayaks. Pushier at high water.

rapids.name: Gunbarrel Rapid
rapids.desc: Read and run; difficult at high water.

rapids.name: Horse Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: At the Horse Creek confluence, between the upper and lower Horse Creek camps.

rapids.name: Stub Creek Rapids
rapids.desc: Read and run at normal and low flows; large waves at high water.

rapids.name: Ranier Rapid
rapids.desc: Big, fun waves. A good last rapid of the day above Alder Creek camp. Hard on inflatable kayaks.

rapids.name: Alder Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Read and run, small splashy waves.

rapids.name: Lantz Rapid
rapids.desc: Enter right of center, then work left past the wall. A large center hole can trouble small craft at some flows.

rapids.name: Devil's Teeth Rapid
rapids.desc: Run between the "molars". Many kayakers swim here. Pictographs just downstream on river left.

rapids.name: Little Devil's Teeth Rapid
rapids.desc: Mile and rating from a single source; verify.

rapids.name: Black Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Created by a debris flow in April 2011 and one of the most powerful rapids on the run. Scout from the left bank; the line changes with water level. It drowned the former Salmon Falls under its pool.

rapids.name: Barth Rapid
rapids.desc: Just below the hot springs. Mile and rating from a single source; verify.

rapids.name: Hancock Rapid
rapids.desc: A large hole low in the rapid, right of center. More action on the right.

rapids.name: Wake Up Rapid (Maisie's)
rapids.desc: Large waves.

rapids.name: Hida Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Read and run.

rapids.name: Andy the Russian Rapid
rapids.desc: At the Bargamin Creek confluence. Very large waves at high water; read and run at lower flows.

rapids.name: Bailey Rapid
rapids.desc: Fun holes, but boats can flip here. An easy hike from Bargamin camp to scout.

rapids.name: Boy Scout Rock
rapids.desc: Known for flips and wraps at certain flows.

rapids.name: Five Mile Rapid
rapids.desc: Hard to spot on entry. Large hole in the center near the bottom; enter left.

rapids.name: Split Rock Rapid
rapids.desc: Pronounced waves and a big hole at high water. Enter right of center.

rapids.name: Stinker Rapid
rapids.desc: Short and sometimes splashy; difficult at low flows.

rapids.name: Big Mallard Rapid
rapids.desc: Probably the most famous rapid on the Main. A large hole that is easy to avoid but requires getting close to it. Trail from Upper Yellow Pine camp to look it over.

rapids.name: Little Mallard Rapid
rapids.desc: Mile and rating from a single source; verify.

rapids.name: Elkhorn Rapid
rapids.desc: The longest rapid on the river. Scout from the left; look for elk antlers in a tree upstream on the left.

rapids.name: Growler Rapid
rapids.desc: Difficult at low flows.

rapids.name: 31 Rapid (Don't Lose Me Now)
rapids.desc: Named for outfitter Bob Smith.

rapids.name: Whiplash Rapid
rapids.desc: Much bigger at high flows; scout. A rock on river right at normal flows.

rapids.name: Reed Riffle
rapids.desc: Read and run.

rapids.name: China Bar Rapid
rapids.desc: Abrupt left turn. Stay inside left; a large shelf in the center can ruin your day.

rapids.name: Big Blowout Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Mile and rating from a single source; verify.

rapids.name: Boise Bar Rapid
rapids.desc: Easy except for a very large hole near the bottom, right of center. Stay left.

rapids.name: Jackson Bar Riffle
rapids.desc: Watch for sleeper holes.

rapids.name: Ludwig Rapid
rapids.desc: The last significant rapid for about 21 miles. Stay left of center and avoid the rocks at the bottom.

rapids.name: Polly Corner
rapids.desc: A jarring right turn with tricky current.

rapids.name: Dried Meat Rapid
rapids.desc: Blasted with dynamite after a 1962 jet boat accident. Big waves today.

rapids.name: Chittam Rapid
rapids.desc: Very difficult at high flows. Keep moving right throughout; scout from river right.

rapids.name: Vinegar Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Steep, and more exciting as the water drops. Stay right for the cleanest line; avoid the large center wave or hole near the bottom.

rapids.name: Carey Falls (Gold Hole)
rapids.desc: Easy to avoid. Going right puts you in one of the larger holes on the river; run left. A popular kayak play hole.

hikes.name: Legend Creek Pictographs
hikes.desc: A short walk, possibly tricky, to pictographs on the wall. Do not touch the paint.

hikes.name: Spindle Creek stone ruins
hikes.desc: Stone ruins from a 1950s settler near the camp.

hikes.name: Devil's Teeth Pictographs
hikes.desc: Pictographs on the rock face just below the lower camp.

hikes.name: Chamberlain Creek trail
hikes.desc: Trail climbing toward Chamberlain Basin, headwaters of Big Creek. Turn around anywhere.

hikes.name: Hot Tub Hot Springs
hikes.desc: A masonry-walled tub reached by climbing rocks. One of the best hot springs in Idaho. No camping or lunch stops.

hikes.name: Barth Hot Springs
hikes.desc: At lower flows, names and dates are scratched into at least six rocks.

hikes.name: Idaho Centennial Trail crossing
hikes.desc: The trail crosses the river corridor here.

hikes.name: Bargamin Creek to scout Bailey
hikes.desc: An easy hike from camp to look over Bailey Rapid.

hikes.name: Mallard viewpoint
hikes.desc: Short trail from Upper Yellow Pine camp to look over Big Mallard.

hikes.name: Campbell's Ferry
hikes.desc: Site of a ferry operated from about 1890 to 1956, once the only dry crossing for 50 miles. The pack bridge is just downstream.

hikes.name: Buckskin Bill's
hikes.desc: Former Five Mile Bar homestead of Sylvan Hart. A small museum and a resupply shop.

hikes.name: Indian Creek Ranch
hikes.desc: A shady trail up Indian Creek from camp.

history: Sylvan Hart homesteaded Five Mile Bar. The gun tower and homestead now hold a small museum and a store.
A ferry ran here from about 1890 to 1956 and was the only dry crossing for 50 miles. The pack bridge that replaced it is named for Frances Zaunmiller Wisner.
In April 2011 a debris flow built the Black Creek rapid and drowned Salmon Falls under its pool.
The rapid was blasted with dynamite after a 1962 jet boat accident that drowned five people.
Legend says a prospector's cache of gold from the bar has never been found.
The Army Corps eyed Black Canyon as a dam site. Wild and Scenic designation in 1980 ended the threat.
The Salmon was called the River of No Return because its rapids made it nearly impossible to travel upstream by boat. Lewis and Clark considered running it in 1805 but turned back.

Congress created the River of No Return Wilderness in 1980 from the older Idaho Primitive Area and other roadless land. It was renamed the Frank Church–River of No Return Wilderness in 1984, and at about 2.3 million acres it is one of the largest wilderness areas in the lower 48. The Salmon flows through the second-deepest gorge on the continent, after the Snake River’s Hells Canyon.

Polly Bemis (1853–1933) was born in China, came to Idaho in the 1870s and made a life on the Salmon River with her husband, Charlie Bemis, on the ranch that carries her name. Her story is one of the best known in the canyon.
indigenous: The Salmon River canyon lies in the homelands of the Nez Perce (Nimiipuu) and of Shoshone bands, including the Tukudika, or “Sheepeaters,” who lived year-round in the rugged mountains. The pictographs at Legend Creek and Devil’s Teeth are reminders of that long presence. Look and photograph, but never touch the paint.
geology: From Black Canyon on, the walls are granite-like rock of the Idaho Batholith, which cooled deep underground in the Cretaceous, roughly 100 to 70 million years ago. Steep, bare slopes and big boulder bars come from this hard rock, and the river carves one of the deepest gorges in North America.
flows: Riverbrain lists a recommended range of about 4,000 to 35,000 cfs for the run. Landings, camps and rapids such as Big Mallard, Black Creek and Chittam change a great deal across that range, so plan for the water you will actually have.

rules.d: A permit is required for float travel on the Wild section of the Main Salmon, upstream of Vinegar Boat Ramp (Corn Creek to Long Tom Bar).

June 20 to September 7. Launches are limited and assigned by lottery; applications are taken December 1 to January 31 on Recreation.gov. Outside the control season permits are still required but launches are not limited.

rules.t: The permit holder must be on the trip
rules.d: Permits are not transferable. The permit holder must be at least 18 on the launch date.
Some camps are reservable and some are first-come. Camp assignments come with the permit packet and are issued at Corn Creek.
A portable toilet system is required. Do not bury waste or use vault toilets for it.
Fire pans and an ash container are required; carry a shovel, bucket and a food strainer for dishwater.
Minimum-impact camping applies throughout the Wild section.

landmarks.name: Corn Creek Boat Ramp
landmarks.desc: Put-in, permit office and gear check. Campground with water and pit toilets next to the ramp.

landmarks.name: Wheat Creek
landmarks.desc: Eastern boundary of the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.

landmarks.name: Stub Creek Outfitters
landmarks.desc: Cabins used by a fishing outfitter. No camping.

landmarks.name: Black Canyon
landmarks.desc: The start of Black Canyon, with the first view of the Idaho Batholith. A 1935 National Geographic expedition passed through here.

landmarks.name: Arctic Creek Lodge
landmarks.desc: Cabins under Forest Service permit, at a former Army Corps dam site. Wild and Scenic designation in 1980 ended the dam threat.

landmarks.name: Sabe Creek
landmarks.desc: Described as one of the prettiest creeks on the river.

landmarks.name: Whitewater Ranch
landmarks.desc: Often used by vehicle campers.

landmarks.name: Campbell Ferry Pack Bridge
landmarks.desc: Frances Zaunmiller Wisner Memorial Pack Bridge, completed in 1956.

landmarks.name: Lemhi Creek
landmarks.desc: Marks China Bar Rapid, just around the corner.

landmarks.name: Wilson Bar Airstrip
landmarks.desc: Completed in 1958; the only public airstrip in the Main Salmon corridor.

landmarks.name: Mackay Bar Airstrip
landmarks.desc: Private airstrip.

landmarks.name: Mackay Bar Ranch
landmarks.desc: Lodging bookable through the ranch.

landmarks.name: South Fork Salmon confluence
landmarks.desc: The South Fork joins on river left. The camp at the mouth is very difficult to reach.

landmarks.name: Diversion Tunnel
landmarks.desc: Tunnel blasted for a mining power project and abandoned in the early 1940s.

landmarks.name: Start of the flat water
landmarks.desc: Long pools and flat water from here to near the take-out.

landmarks.name: Shepp Ranch
landmarks.desc: Private ranch.

landmarks.name: Polly Bemis Ranch
landmarks.desc: Private ranch on river left, historic home of Polly Bemis.

landmarks.name: Long Tom Creek
landmarks.desc: End of the permitted Wild section, named for a mining sluice tool.

landmarks.name: Vinegar Creek Boat Ramp
landmarks.desc: Narrow ramp used mostly by jet boats; limited parking.

landmarks.name: Wind River Pack Bridge
landmarks.desc: Rebuilt in 1962. A 24-mile trail starts here.

notes.camp: *Reservable camps are marked on the permit; other camps are first come. Landings are difficult at high flows, and several large bars are not reachable at the top of the runoff. Rattlesnakes, ticks and poison ivy are common around camps.
notes.hike: *Look at pictographs, ruins and old homesteads but never touch or take anything. Trails are steep and hot in summer, with rattlesnakes and poison ivy.

access.name: Salmon
access.note: Nearest town to the put-in; permits are issued by the Salmon-Challis River Office

access.name: Corn Creek
access.note: Put-in. Campground, water, toilets, permit office

access.name: Mackay Bar
access.note: Private airstrip and ranch; Painter Mine Road reaches the bridge camp

access.name: Vinegar Creek
access.note: Alternate take-out; narrow ramp, jet boat traffic, limited parking

access.name: Carey Creek
access.note: Take-out. Large lot, paved ramps, toilet

permit.status: Required year-round · lottery June 20 to Sept 7

items.d: Apply on Recreation.gov for control-season dates (June 20 to September 7). Aggregator sites report applications December 1 to January 31 and results mid-February; confirm on the permit page.
Add group members, watercraft, launch and exit dates and pay fees on Recreation.gov no later than 7 days before launch.
Call or email the Salmon-Challis River Office at least 4 days before launch to confirm the reservation is finalized.
The office emails the permit. Print it, sign it and carry it for the whole trip. The Recreation.gov reservation is not the permit.
A permit is still required, and launches are not limited.
June 20 to September 7.
Control season: 21 days before launch, by 11:59 p.m. Mountain. Outside it: 3 days before.
$6, non-refundable.
$4 per person per day.
1 to 10 people: up to 8 days. 11 to 20: up to 7 days. 21 to 30: up to 6 days.
Up to 30 people and 10 days.
Large camps are reserved for groups of 21 or more. You must camp at reserved camps on the listed dates.
A late cancellation or no-show brings a three-year ban on holding a permit or applying for this river. There is no penalty if water at Corn Creek is above 5.0 feet.
Check the Recreation.gov calendar for the number of groups booked on each date.

stats.season: Lottery season runs June 20 to September 7. Runoff usually peaks in early June.

flow.note: Another guide lists 2,000 to 23,000 cfs at the White Bird gauge, so check which gauge a number refers to. Spring flows often top 23,000 in May and June.
